parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a functioning rule-of-law state with no documented traveler-facing exposure: no trans-specific criminal statute, no border/document friction, no police profiling, no facility restrictions (bathroom access protected), and no custody-placement record. Gender identity is covered by the Gender Equality Act and courts have actually enforced LGBTI-protective outcomes. State response to the single documented trans killing (2022) was positive: 12-year sentence, provocation rejected. What holds the score below the 0.85 band is the absence of hate-crime/hate-speech coverage for gender identity, LGBTIQ-wide elevated avoidance behaviours (hand-holding, location avoidance) signalling residual public hostility, one documented murder, and unresolved questions (action-plan implementation, self-ID intent). Social climate is mixed rather than hostile; no universal-exposure measures exist.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; no mismatch questioning, secondary screening, or refusal of entry reported for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Recognition machinery exists but is resident-facing; visitor documents are untouched by it.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented interaction between visitor documents and border officials.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented trans-specific detention or custody-placement practice; 2018 compliance report scope includes safety of LGBT people deprived of liberty but findings not detailed.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Functioning courts shown remedying LGBTI discrimination.

federal_state_facilities.protection: Bathroom access is protected per the comparative index; no facility exclusion documented.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; no refusal of care or medication confiscation cases.
care_services.protection: Healthcare anti-discrimination law covers gender identity (barometer, 2011–2024).
care_services.interaction: Resident LGR pathway (medical-diagnosis-gated) does not reach visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: One 2023 assault at a community bar — but police arrested the perpetrator; no state threat-framing documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Police act on anti-LGBTI violence; ministers attended Pride 2023; foreign ministry aligns with regional LGBTI advocacy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Deportation penalty for the 2023 assailant shows enforcement seriousness.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented; no age-dependent traveler rule recorded.
minors_guardians.protection: Minors have access to puberty blockers domestically (resident-facing climate signal).

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Single documented trans murder (2022, Jamaican trans woman, 34+ stab wounds); 2007 Pride attacks; LGBTIQ-wide 40% avoid locations for fear of assault.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Killer sentenced to 12 years, provocation rejected; 2023 bar assailant arrested; Pride resumed and state-backed.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Single case is weak rate evidence in a medium country; response was protective.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No hate-crime/hate-speech protection for gender identity; conversion therapy not banned; unresolved self-ID and action-plan implementation; survey avoidance figures are LGBTIQ-wide and pre-2024.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts remedy discrimination (festival funding, partnership registration); equality law enforced in employment.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Supranational machinery partially offsets thin national hate-crime recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vessalia documents recent enforcement successes (apologies, compensation, disciplined officers) against visitor-facing friction. Here no visitor friction is documented at all, but hate-crime law is absent, avoidance behaviours are elevated, and one killing stands; slightly below 0.85.

Alderland's profile — protections with occasional late-night attacks and uneven police responsiveness — closely matches this dossier. Here the documented police response is stronger (sentence, arrests, ministerial backing), but hate-crime coverage for gender identity is missing; roughly at or marginally above the 0.75 anchor level.

Vellmaris documents an actual visitor stop over document-appearance mismatch despite national equality law. No such traveler-facing incident is documented here, and institutional LGBTI alignment is stronger; clearly above 0.65.
Kestrel Isles shows routine secondary screening and discretionary refusal of visitors. Nothing comparable exists in this dossier; well above 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines near-zero documented traveler-facing exposure with a mixed but improving social climate. No law or practice reaches the trans visitor at the border, in facilities, in custody, or in care; bathroom access is protected; police and courts demonstrably act against anti-LGBTI violence (12-year sentence, arrests, rejected provocation). Weighing against: no hate-crime/hate-speech recognition of gender identity, one lethal attack within the documented window, and LGBTIQ-wide survey avoidance above regional averages — genuine social-hostility residue, though not trans-specific or current, and partly mitigated by state alignment with LGBTI advocacy. The unresolved questions (self-ID, action-plan enactment) are open questions, not exposures. Net: solidly in the Reduced Risk band, below jurisdictions documenting working trans-specific hate-crime enforcement.
